english.title: Destruction / redispatch other than in accordance with the authorisation

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: trade in animals and related products regulations 2011

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed to

(A)_[destroy]_
(B)_[redispatch]_

(C)_[a product,]_
(D)_[products,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE PRODUCT(S)..), to which Part 3 of the Trade in Animals and Related Products Regulations 2011 would otherwise have applied, which was

(E)_[sent as a trade sample]_
(F)_[intended for exhibition]_
(G)_[intended for particular studies or analyses]_

(H)_[when the exhibition was finished,]_
(I)_[when the particular studies or analyses had been carried out,]_

as specified in the import authorisation
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 4(3) of Schedule 3 to and regulations 39 and 42(2) of the Trade in Animals and Related Products Regulations 2011.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
failed to destroy / redispatch a product
sent as trade sample / intended for exhibition / studies or analyses
when the exhibition was finished / studies or analyses carried out
as specified in the import authorisation

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
